title: Transfer of the fixed-G1-invert STNFS core to bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain at 125.3306834

claims.statement: For the production bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain target, the algorithm in proof.md returns the canonical scalar x for uniform T=[x]P0 with success at least 0.39 conditional on the core's explicitly disclosed H1-H5 heuristics in source-core.md. The reduction is z=e(T,Q0)=e(P0,Q0)^x, so the fixed-G1-invert core e3940d11 (declared 2^121.9944 at C=20000) recovers x. Total cold classical work, including the core's preprocessing, both logs, all failures and the wrapper, is bounded by 2^125.3306834 target-operation units at C=2000: the core term is multiplied by 101/100 as a conservative implementation-price reserve and by 10 for the C=20000 to C=2000 conversion, and the 2^80 wrapper term is divided by 2000. Peak storage is below 2^106 bytes, preprocessing is bounded by the full total, no external advice or cross-target amortization is assumed. The complete inherited core evidence is supplied unchanged; no prior review verdict is a premise. This is an analytic exploratory claim, not a full-size run; the conversion arithmetic and distribution argument do not establish the inherited kernel or NFS premises.

experiments.purpose: Runs the supplied core's twenty-one evidence checks unchanged (resultant, tower, rho/pool, nbar, linear-algebra loop, ball counts, relation inputs, work allowance, declared bounds, alpha, missing logs, record widths, descent-plan feasibility, audit, retention, ECM, field checks, feasible, within_claim, success_ok), then the transfer checks: the toy bijections over (Z/r)^*, the recover_p budget, the g1_plain budget against the declared ceiling, and the success lower model. Neither part validates the inherited production heuristics.
